name: operators
title: Operators and precedence
summary: Seven formulas over two exported variables (a = 7, b = 3) with their live results: precedence, parentheses, left-to-right evaluation, float division, % and unary minus.
prompt: Show a small cheat sheet of arithmetic formulas over a = 7 and b = 3 (a + b * 2, (a + b) * 2, a - b - 1, a / b, a % b, -a % b, -b * -2) with each computed result next to it.
teaches: Write a value as an infix formula string over @variables: "@a + @b * 2" compiles to one float expression that re-evaluates when a or b changes
Rely on the usual precedence (* / % before + -, unary minus binds tightest) and group with parentheses; equal operators run left to right
Expect % to truncate like Java's float %: the result takes the sign of the left operand, so -7 % 3 is -1, not 2
pitfalls: The infix parser knows only + - * / % and unary minus: no ^, no comparison (<, >, ==) and no && or ||; write pow(x, n), and step() or ifElse() for comparisons (EXP-06)
Write a variable as @name; a bare name also resolves when it is declared, but bare width and height mean componentWidth() and componentHeight(), so don't name your own variables that and drop the @
-3 directly after an operator, a comma or a parenthesis is folded into a negative literal; -@b is a CHANGE_SIGN operation on the variable
A device reader refuses an expression longer than 32 RPN tokens (numbers, variables, operators and functions each count); split a long formula into named resources.variables

When a row of formula, result and note no longer fits, a plain row squeezes the last child to 0 wide: make it a collapsibleRow and give the note a collapsiblePriority (1) so it is the one dropped; unprioritized children are kept first

snippets.note: a exported (export: true) so the host can change it; every formula below follows
-@a % @b → -1: % keeps the sign of the left side
textFromFloat with decimal 2 and flags 7 shows 2.33

check.describe: Seven rows read 13, 20, 3, 2.33, 1, -1 and 6. Resized, the rows fill the width; each row is a collapsibleRow whose note has the lowest priority, so at 234 wide the notes are dropped while every formula keeps its result, and at 540 the notes have room to spare.
